slides.body: Every synthetic download time increases by 10 seconds.

slides.question: How does the standard deviation change?

slides.title: Distance in standard deviations
slides.body: A z-score measures distance from a mean in standard-deviation units. Synthetic sizes have mean 40 KB and SD 5 KB.
slides.question: How many standard deviations above the mean is 55 KB?

slides.title: Below the mean
slides.body: Synthetic response times have mean 20 seconds and standard deviation 4 seconds.
slides.question: What standardized distance corresponds to 12 seconds?

slides.title: Recovering a data value
slides.body: Synthetic times have mean 20 seconds and standard deviation 4 seconds.
slides.question: What value lies 1.5 standard deviations below the mean?

slides.title: Compare relative positions
slides.body: Synthetic quiz A: mean 70, SD 5, score 80. Quiz B: mean 60, SD 10, score 80.
slides.question: Which score is farther above its mean in standard-deviation units?

slides.title: Sampling variability of a statistic
slides.body: Sampling variability is how a statistic changes across repeated samples. Its standard deviation is called its standard error.
slides.question: Does standard error describe the spread of individual observations or of statistics?

slides.title: Standard error of the mean
slides.body: For independent observations with population SD σ, the standard error of the sample mean is σ/√n.
slides.question: If σ = 12 seconds and n = 36, what is the standard error?

slides.title: Chebyshev’s bound
slides.body: For any distribution with finite, positive variance, at least 1 − 1/k² lies within k standard deviations of the mean, k > 1.
slides.question: What minimum fraction lies within two standard deviations?

slides.title: Empirical rule
slides.body: For an approximately bell-shaped distribution, about 68%, 95%, and 99.7% lie within one, two, and three standard deviations.
slides.question: With mean 50 and SD 4, what interval contains about 95%?
